rows.label: WELLBYs per standard-deviation-year of improvement in wellbeing or depression measures

source.title: HLI, StrongMinds and Friendship Bench CEA (Nov 2024 update), summary spreadsheet V4

rows.explainer:
Converts an effect measured in standard deviations (SDs) of a depression or wellbeing scale into WELLBYs: points of life satisfaction (0–10) for one year. HLI uses 2: one SD of life satisfaction in low-income samples is about two points.

The ±25% range is ours. HLI's point value hides the debate over whether depression scales and life satisfaction move one for one.

rows.label: Household size of psychotherapy recipients (HLI)

source.title: HLI, StrongMinds and Friendship Bench CEA (Nov 2024 update), summary spreadsheet V4

rows.explainer: Average household size, including the person treated, in the settings HLI models (Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Replace it with a country fact when the charity works elsewhere.

rows.label: Household spillover of psychotherapy, as a share of the recipient's own effect

source.title: HLI, StrongMinds and Friendship Bench CEA (Nov 2024 update), summary spreadsheet V4

rows.explainer: How much each other household member benefits when one person is treated, relative to the person treated. HLI's 16% rests on a handful of studies. The range is ours: below 5% the spillover is negligible; 30% is about what HLI estimated for cash transfers.

rows.label: Units of value per WELLBY at which depression counts the same as by its GBD weights (the WELLBY slider's default)

source.title: charityevals' calibration (docs/normalization.md 2.3)
source.note: PHQ-9 SD 4.211710187 (depression.phq9_sd) × 0.031 healthy years per PHQ-9 point-year (depression.dalys_per_phq9_point_year) × 2 units of value per healthy year (the default of "Healthy year vs doubled-income year") ÷ 2 WELLBYs per SD-year (wellby_factors.wellbys_per_sd_year) = 0.130563. src/engine/wellby-calibration.test.ts fails if it drifts from those figures or from the slider's default.

rows.explainer:
The rate at which one standard deviation of depression for a year is worth the same whether it goes through HLI's WELLBYs (2 WELLBYs) or through the Global Burden of Disease weights on the PHQ-9 (4.2 points × 0.031 = 0.13 healthy years): 0.13 doubled-income years per WELLBY, the default of the WELLBY slider.

HLI models that count deaths read it once, to put a death valued the site's way (GiveWell's moral weights by age, times the value-of-life slider) into WELLBYs: at the slider's default such a death counts exactly what it counts in every other model. A model row may not read the slider itself (the exchange rate belongs to the unit's conversion), so the anchor stands in for it.
